Profile-likelihood interval for a Gaussian smoothing scale

Source: R/gaussian_scale_profile.R
gaussian_scale_profile.Rd

Fixes one scale at each grid value and reoptimizes all remaining conductance and measurement parameters on the fitted graph.

Usage

gaussian_scale_profile(fit, layer, n = 25, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fit

An unslimmed Gaussian scale fit with its original model closures.

layer

Name of the raster layer whose scale is profiled.

n

Number of grid points across the fitted scale bounds, at least five. The fitted estimate is also included if it is not already on the grid.

level

Confidence level between zero and one.

Value

A list with layer, estimate, level, interval, grid, and fit. The grid contains scale values and profile log likelihoods. The returned fit stores the interval, so confint(result$fit) uses it at the matching level.

Details

The interval is the connected likelihood-ratio support region containing the fitted estimate, using the one-degree-of-freedom chi-square cutoff. Grid crossings are refined by root finding. Increase n to check for additional support regions. Limits stop at the original bounds. At a boundary the usual chi-square calibration is an approximation. Failed optimizations stop the calculation instead of silently dropping profile points. Both conductance and final measurement-parameter convergence are required. This can be substantially slower than Wald intervals.

Worked example

See vignette("v07-gaussian-scale-optimization", package = "terradish") for scale profiles, forest-effect plots, and interpretation in map units.

See also

gaussian_scale_summary, gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance, terradish_inference

Other spatial scale: gaussian_scale_summary(), gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(), terradish_scale_optim()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(24)
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, xmin = 0, xmax = 10,
                 ymin = 0, ymax = 10, crs = "EPSG:3857")
terra::values(r) <- rnorm(100)
names(r) <- "x"
graph <- conductance_surface(r, terra::xyFromCell(r, seq(3, 98, 5)),
                             directions = 4)
factory <- gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(graph,
  sigma_lower = 0.4, sigma_upper = 1.5)
response <- simulate_covariance_response(c(x = 0.7, sigma.x = 0.8),
  ~x, graph, conductance_model = factory, tau = 1, sigma = 0.1,
  nu = 10000, seed = 14)$covariance
fit <- terradish(response ~ x, graph, conductance_model = factory,
  measurement_model = wishart_covariance, nu = 10000, optimizer = "newton")
profile <- gaussian_scale_profile(fit, "x", n = 5)
profile$interval
#>     lower     upper 
#> 0.7807026 0.8396359 
confint(profile$fit)
#>             2.5 %    97.5 %
#> x       0.6780223 0.7157837
#> sigma.x 0.7807026 0.8396359
#> attr(,"note")
#> [1] "Stored Gaussian profile intervals are used where available; remaining scale intervals are truncated Wald intervals."
# The stored profile interval replaces the matching scale Wald interval.
# }
